newsitem.title: USA: Partygoers irate after the big inaugural bash.
newsitem.headline: Partygoers irate after the big inaugural bash.

text.p: President Bill Clinton happily danced the night away at a series of glittering inaugural balls, but once he left, partygoers early on Tuesday found themselves turned into Cinderellas who had to scream, shout and shove to get their coats.

Well after the clock struck midnight at one prominent hotel, hundreds of angry partygoers celebrating the start of Clinton's second term in the White House -- tired men in tuxedoes and equally exhausted women in long gowns -- found themselves waiting for hours to get into a coat check room.
"Everybody tried to get their coats at once," said a hotel executive as witnesses talked of police blowing ear-piercing whistles and using bullhorns to appeal for calm at the Omni Shoreham hotel.
The angry crowd responded with pushing, shoving and chants of "We want our coats," witnesses said. Some women got so tired that they simply went to sleep on the floor.

Instead of just nursing hangovers, many partygoers nursed grudges at their inability to ride the president's coattails for a carefree night on the town. And in revenge they bombarded talk shows with complaints.

Besides the coatroom debacle at the Omni Shoreham, which held three balls including the large Mid-Atlantic States gala, there were complaints about long lines trying to get into "oversold" balls at other locations and high prices being charged for food and drink.
Tickets for the 15 inaugural balls cost $150 each and for an extra $5.50 you could also get a ham or turkey roll.

Vice President Al Gore's sister-in-law was trapped in the cold with several hundred others outside Union Station for over an hour because of the long time it took to get through metal detectors, the Washington Post said.
President Clinton, First Lady Hillary Clinton and their daughter Chelsea appeared briefly at each of the galas held in their honour but stayed at some for only 10 minutes.
They were home in bed at the White House before 2 a.m. (0700 GMT) , something many people who attended the Mid-Atlantic States ball were not able to say.

Craig Sundall, director of marketing for the hotel, blamed the problem on "compression" saying thousands of people at the three balls in the hotel started leaving at the same time once the president left.
"There were challenges getting coats, but there was no riot" he said, adding that the probem continued through the night.
